title: Yellow low-battery indicator
shortDescription: Battery below ~20% — charge before next brushing.
fullDescription:
Philips Sonicare shows a solid yellow light when battery is low and a flashing yellow when critically low. The brush will still run for a short time.

Replace on inductive charger until a steady green light appears, typically 24 hours for a full charge.

fixSteps.title: Place on charger
fixSteps.instruction: Return brush to inductive base.

fixSteps.title: Charge 24 hours
fixSteps.instruction: Wait for steady green LED or none (fully charged).

whenToCallPro: If runtime falls below 3 days with full charge.

faq.q: Can I brush with yellow light?

title: BrushSync head replacement alert
shortDescription: Smart brush head reports end-of-life via RFID.
fullDescription:
DiamondClean and 9900 Prestige heads contain BrushSync RFID. After approximately 3 months of use the brush emits three beeps and flashes an icon to replace the head.

Insert a new Sonicare G3, C3, or W3 smart head to reset the counter.

fixSteps.title: Buy genuine head
fixSteps.instruction: G3 Premium Gum Care, C3 Premium Plaque, or W3 Premium White.

fixSteps.title: Pull off old head
fixSteps.instruction: Pull straight up on the old head.

fixSteps.title: Click new head
fixSteps.instruction: Align and press until RFID registers — counter resets automatically.

faq.q: Can I reset BrushSync without new head?

title: Runtime reduced to days or less
shortDescription: Li-ion battery at end of life after 3-5 years.
fullDescription:
Sonicare Li-ion cells typically last 3-5 years. Degradation shows as short runtime, inability to hold charge, and constant yellow indicator.

Philips does not service the battery on most models; the brush must be replaced or recycled.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Run to full discharge then full charge once.

fixSteps.title: Measure runtime
fixSteps.instruction: Count brushings before yellow recurs.

fixSteps.title: Consider replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Battery is not user-serviceable — plan for new brush.

whenToCallPro: Philips support may replace under warranty if within 2 years.

faq.a: Only destructively — not worth it vs new brush.

title: Brush not charging on base
shortDescription: Misaligned brush, bad contact, or failed charger.
fullDescription:
The inductive charger requires precise alignment. If no LED activity when placed, try another outlet and ensure the brush is centered.

On DiamondClean glass charger, ensure the brush sits on the coil at the base of the glass.

fixSteps.title: Reposition brush
fixSteps.instruction: Center brush on charger coil.

fixSteps.title: Swap outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Verify outlet is live.

fixSteps.title: Wait 15 minutes
fixSteps.instruction: Very drained battery needs warm-up before LED shows.

whenToCallPro: If new charger also fails to charge brush.

faq.a: Most HX series share chargers, but verify voltage.

title: Brush vibration feels weak or slow
shortDescription: Worn head, low battery, or motor magnet shift.
fullDescription:
The sonic motor runs at 31,000 strokes per minute. Weak vibration can be a worn head (less mass), low battery, or a magnet displacement from a drop.

Install new head and fully charge before concluding motor failure.

fixSteps.title: New head
fixSteps.instruction: Install a genuine Sonicare head.

fixSteps.title: Full charge
fixSteps.instruction: Charge 24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Verify vibration
fixSteps.instruction: Compare hand-feel against fresh brush video.

whenToCallPro: If weak after new head and full charge.

title: Vibration intensity ramps up over 14 sessions
shortDescription: EasyStart feature gradually increases power — not a fault.
fullDescription:
Sonicare's EasyStart lowers power for the first 14 brushings so new users can adapt. This is normal, not a defect.

Disable via the Sonicare app or turn off by holding the power button specifically per model.

fixSteps.title: Continue brushing
fixSteps.instruction: EasyStart auto-ends after 14 full 2-minute sessions.

fixSteps.title: Disable in app
fixSteps.instruction: In Sonicare app, toggle EasyStart off.

title: Purple pressure feedback active
shortDescription: Brush detecting excess pressure on teeth.
fullDescription:
DiamondClean Smart and 9900 Prestige include a pressure sensor that lights purple and reduces vibration when you press too hard. Not a fault but a coaching feature.

Ease pressure and let the sonic motion do the work.

fixSteps.title: Reduce pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Guide brush with fingertips, not palm.

fixSteps.title: Watch app coaching
fixSteps.instruction: Open app for real-time pressure graph.

faq.a: No, it's always on for safety.

title: Brush does not respond to power button
shortDescription: Usually discharged battery — charge 24 hours before declaring dead.
fullDescription:
Sonicare Li-ion batteries in full discharge require a trickle wake-up. Place on charger for 24 hours before concluding the unit is dead.

If there is still no response, the battery management system has locked out.

fixSteps.title: Long charge
fixSteps.instruction: Leave on charger 24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Try different charger
fixSteps.instruction: Borrow another HX base to rule out charger fault.

fixSteps.title: Contact Philips
fixSteps.instruction: If still dead, request warranty replacement.

whenToCallPro: Dead after extended charge + alternative charger.

title: Sonicare app cannot sync session
shortDescription: Bluetooth or account issue preventing session upload.
fullDescription:
The Sonicare app records sessions over Bluetooth. If sync fails, check that the brush has unsynced history (hold mode), then reconnect via the app's connect flow.

Log out and back into your Philips account if persistent.

fixSteps.title: Reconnect
fixSteps.instruction: Tap brush icon in app and follow reconnect flow.

fixSteps.title: Restart Bluetooth
fixSteps.instruction: Toggle Bluetooth off/on.

fixSteps.title: Re-login
fixSteps.instruction: Log out Philips account and back in.

faq.q: How long is session history stored?
faq.a: About 14 sessions on brush before overwrite.

title: Mode button not changing settings
shortDescription: Silicone overlay stuck or firmware locked.
fullDescription: If the mode/intensity button doesn't cycle through settings, either the button is gummed with toothpaste residue or firmware is locked on single mode. Clean around the button and long-press power+mode to reset.

fixSteps.title: Clean button area
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe around button with damp microfibre.

fixSteps.title: Hold reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press power+mode together for 15 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Charge and retest
fixSteps.instruction: Place on charger briefly and test buttons.

faq.q: Can I open it to clean inside?
faq.a: No — opening voids warranty and risks water seal.
